options.text: This deployment creates Azure Files or Azure NetApp Files storage for FSLogix profile containers. It automates the applicable storage identity configuration, domain integration, share-level access, private networking, and NTFS permissions that otherwise require manual setup.

Before deployment, verify that the deployment principal has the required resource and role-assignment permissions and that the selected subscription, networking, identity, and supporting services meet the prerequisites for your configuration. Review the complete prerequisite checklist before continuing.

elements.name: resourceScope
elements.instanceDetailsLabel: FSLogix Storage Location and Resource Group

location.label: Region
location.toolTip: Select the Azure region for FSLogix storage and the temporary deployment resources.

elements.name: storageAssociation
elements.label: FSLogix Storage Purpose
elements.toolTip: Choose whether this storage supports one host pool persona or is shared by multiple host pools. This choice controls host pool association and naming defaults.

allowedValues.label: Shared across host pools
allowedValues.description: Deploy storage for multiple host pools. Use a stable identifier describing the shared user population; no host pool parent tag is applied.

allowedValues.label: Host pool-specific - existing persona
allowedValues.description: Associate storage with an existing host pool. Its persona identifier and naming convention are offered as editable defaults, and its resource ID is applied as the parent tag.

allowedValues.label: Host pool-specific - future persona
allowedValues.description: Deploy storage before its host pool. Enter the exact persona identifier that the future host pool will use.

elements.name: hostPool
elements.label: Associated Host Pool
elements.toolTip: Select the host pool for this persona-specific storage. Its resource ID is applied as the cm-resource-parent tag for cost allocation and resource governance.

constraints.allowedValues: [map(steps('scope').storagePurpose.hostPoolsApi.value, (hp) => parse(concat('{"label":"', hp.name, '","description":"Resource Group: ', first(skip(split(hp.id, '/'), 4)), '","value":{"id":"', hp.id, '","name":"', hp.name, '"}}')))]

options.text: First select how the session hosts that consume this storage are joined. AD DS and Microsoft Entra Domain Services directly determine Azure Files authentication. Microsoft Entra-joined hosts can use storage account keys or Microsoft Entra Kerberos. The join type also determines storage-service availability: Azure NetApp Files is available only with AD DS; all other paths use Azure Files.

elements.name: machineIdentity
elements.label: Session Host Join Type
elements.toolTip: Select how the session hosts that consume this storage are joined. This determines the supported storage services and Azure Files authentication methods.

allowedValues.label: Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS)
allowedValues.description: Session hosts are joined to AD DS and require network connectivity to domain controllers. Azure Files uses AD DS authentication. Azure NetApp Files is also available.

allowedValues.label: Microsoft Entra Domain Services
allowedValues.description: Session hosts are joined to a Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain. Azure Files uses Entra Domain Services authentication.

allowedValues.label: Microsoft Entra joined
allowedValues.description: Session hosts are Microsoft Entra joined. Azure Files can use storage account keys or Microsoft Entra Kerberos. Azure NetApp Files is not available.

elements.name: identitySolution
elements.label: Azure Files Authentication Method
elements.toolTip: Select how Microsoft Entra-joined session hosts authenticate to Azure Files.

allowedValues.label: Storage account key
allowedValues.description: Azure Files access uses the storage account key. No Kerberos identity configuration is required, and sharding is not supported.

allowedValues.label: Microsoft Entra Kerberos for cloud-only identities
allowedValues.description: For cloud-only Microsoft Entra identities and Microsoft Entra-joined clients. Supports identity-based permissions and sharding.

allowedValues.label: Microsoft Entra Kerberos for hybrid identities
allowedValues.description: For identities synchronized from AD DS and Microsoft Entra-joined clients. Requires AD DS and synchronization to Microsoft Entra ID.

elements.name: organizationalUnitPath
elements.label: Storage Computer Object OU Path
elements.toolTip: Enter the distinguished name of the organizational unit for Azure Files storage account computer objects or the Azure NetApp Files Active Directory connection.

constraints.validationMessage: Provide a valid OU path in distinguished name format.

elements.name: credentialSource
elements.label: Domain Credential Source
elements.toolTip: Choose whether to read DomainJoinUserPrincipalName and DomainJoinUserPassword from Key Vault or enter them for this deployment.

options.text: Select a Key Vault containing DomainJoinUserPrincipalName and DomainJoinUserPassword. The temporary VM uses an internally generated local administrator password that is never exposed as a form input or deployment output.

elements.name: credentialsKeyVault
elements.label: Deployment Credentials Key Vault
elements.toolTip: Select the Key Vault containing DomainJoinUserPrincipalName and DomainJoinUserPassword.

elements.name: domainJoinUserPrincipalName
elements.label: Domain Join Account User Principal Name
elements.toolTip: Enter the user principal name of an account with permission to create or join computer objects in the selected OU.

constraints.validationMessage: Provide a valid user principal name.

elements.name: domainJoinUserPassword
elements.toolTip: Enter the password for the domain join account.

options.text: Entra Kerberos automation updates each storage account application manifest, enables cloud group SIDs for cloud-only identities, and grants delegated Microsoft Graph consent. Select an existing user-assigned identity with Microsoft Graph application permissions Application.ReadWrite.All and DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All. Multifactor authentication exclusions remain a manual task.

elements.name: automateEntraKerberosTasks
elements.label: Use a managed identity to automate Entra Kerberos application and consent tasks

elements.name: appUpdateIdentity
elements.label: Entra Kerberos Application Update Identity
elements.toolTip: Select an identity in the deployment region with Microsoft Graph Application.ReadWrite.All and DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All application permissions.

options.text: Choose which users can create FSLogix profile folders. Standard access grants Authenticated Users permission to create a folder at the storage root, while Creator Owner permissions isolate each user's profile contents. Select group-scoped access to limit profile creation to members of the selected groups.

elements.name: leastPrivilegedNtfs
elements.label: Restrict NTFS access to selected groups

options.text: Sharding deploys one Azure Files storage account per selected user group to distribute profile load. Sharding via Permissions relies on share and NTFS permissions. Sharding via Object Specific Settings requires corresponding FSLogix object-specific registry configuration and is not offered for Microsoft Entra Kerberos.

constraints.allowedValues: [if(and(equals(steps('identity').machineIdentity, 'EntraID'), contains(steps('identity').identitySolution, 'EntraKerberos')), parse('[{"label":"No Sharding","value":"None"},{"label":"Sharding via Permissions","value":"ShardPerms"}]'), parse('[{"label":"No Sharding","value":"None"},{"label":"Sharding via Permissions","value":"ShardPerms"},{"label":"Sharding via Object Specific Settings","value":"ShardOSS"}]'))]

options.text: Azure Files share-level RBAC for cloud-only identities, required for group-scoped NTFS access and profile sharding, is available only in supported Azure Commercial regions and is not currently supported in Azure Government. Verify regional availability before deployment.

options.text: Hybrid Entra Kerberos does not domain-join the storage account or temporary VM. Selecting group-scoped NTFS access or sharding via permissions requires the temporary deployment VM to have network line of sight to an AD DS domain controller. The supplied AD credentials are used only to look up the on-premises SIDs of the selected synchronized groups before applying NTFS permissions. An authenticated account with read access to the domain is sufficient.

elements.name: hybridDomainName

constraints.validationMessage: Provide a valid fully qualified domain name.

elements.name: hybridAdLookupUserPrincipalName

constraints.validationMessage: Provide a valid user principal name.

elements.name: hybridAdLookupPassword
elements.toolTip: Enter the password for the AD lookup account.

options.text: Configure encryption, private access, monitoring, and recovery controls for the FSLogix storage deployment.

Azure Files is encrypted at rest with platform-managed keys by default. For customer-managed keys, select an existing Key Vault. The deployment creates one indexed key per storage account, creates a storage encryption identity, and grants that identity key-scoped encryption access.

elements.name: existingEncryptionKeyVault
elements.label: Existing Encryption Key Vault
elements.toolTip: Select the existing Key Vault where the deployment will create one encryption key per Azure Files storage account.

elements.name: keyExpirationInDays
elements.label: Encryption Key Rotation (in Days)
elements.toolTip: Days before a new key version is automatically generated in the selected Key Vault.

options.text: Private endpoints keep Azure Files traffic on private network paths. When private endpoints are enabled without permitted public IP ranges, public network access is disabled.

elements.label: Private Endpoint Virtual Network
elements.toolTip: Select the virtual network where the Azure Files private endpoints will be created.

options.text: A temporary virtual machine and managed identity are required to initialize root NTFS permissions for every storage option. Domain-backed and Entra Kerberos configurations also use the VM for identity setup. Cleanup removes external role assignments and deletes the temporary resource group after configuration completes.

elements.name: deploymentVirtualNetwork
elements.label: Temporary Deployment VM Virtual Network
elements.toolTip: Select the virtual network for the temporary deployment VM.

constraints.allowedValues: [map(filter(steps('scope').virtualNetworksApi.value, (vnet) => equals(vnet.location, steps('scope').resourceScope.location.name)), (vnet) => parse(concat('{"label":"', vnet.name, '","description":"Location: ', vnet.location, ' Resource Group: ', first(skip(split(vnet.id, '/'), 4)), '","value":{"name":"', vnet.name, '","id":"', vnet.id, '"}}')))]

elements.label: Temporary Deployment VM Subnet
elements.toolTip: Select a subnet with network line of sight to domain controllers and private storage endpoints when required.

elements.name: deploymentVirtualMachineOrganizationalUnitPath
elements.label: Temporary Deployment VM OU Path
elements.toolTip: Enter the distinguished name of the organizational unit where the temporary Azure NetApp Files deployment VM is joined.

constraints.validationMessage: Provide a valid OU path in distinguished name format.

elements.name: deploymentVirtualMachineSize
elements.label: Temporary Deployment VM Size
elements.toolTip: Select the size of the temporary deployment virtual machine (2 vCPUs, available in your subscription). This VM is automatically deleted after deployment completes.

options.text: Resource names use the shared FederalAVD naming engine. The standard convention is resource type, workload, purpose, and region. When an existing FederalAVD host pool is selected, its stored naming convention can be used as the starting convention. Individual resource-name overrides remain available for exceptions.

Host Pool Persona is the same identifier used on the host pool form. It represents the distinct user group served by the host pool. Selecting an existing FederalAVD host pool reads its hpIdentifier tag as an editable default; for a future host pool, enter the exact persona value that host pool will use.

elements.name: existingHostPoolPersona
elements.label: Host Pool Persona
elements.toolTip: The selected FederalAVD host pool's hpIdentifier tag is offered as an editable default. This field uses the same constraints as Host Pool Persona in the host-pool form.

validations.message: The identifier must begin and end with an alphanumeric character and can only contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, dashes, and dots.

elements.name: futureHostPoolPersona
elements.label: Host Pool Persona
elements.toolTip: Enter the exact short Host Pool Persona value that the future host pool will use. This field uses the same constraints as Host Pool Persona in the host-pool form.

validations.message: The identifier must begin and end with an alphanumeric character and can only contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, dashes, and dots.

elements.name: sharedStorageIdentifier
elements.label: Shared Storage Identifier
elements.toolTip: The default fslogix identifier follows the fixed purpose-token pattern used by shared monitoring, operations, control-plane, and image-management resources. Change it only to distinguish multiple shared FSLogix storage scopes.

validations.message: The identifier must begin and end with an alphanumeric character and can only contain alphanumeric characters, underscores, dashes, and dots.

elements.name: useHostPoolNamingConvention
elements.label: Use the selected host pool naming convention
elements.toolTip: Uses the hpNamingConvention tag stored on the selected FederalAVD host pool. Clear this option to use the standard FederalAVD convention instead.

options.text: The selected host pool does not contain a FederalAVD hpNamingConvention tag. Generated names will use the standard FederalAVD convention unless you provide individual overrides.

Each field shows the standard generated name as a placeholder. Leave a field blank to use the naming engine. In placeholders, {identifier}, {location}, {unique}, and {vmName} describe generated values and should be replaced in explicit names. In private endpoint conventions, RESOURCE, SUBRESOURCE, and VNETID are required runtime tokens and must remain in the entered convention.

elements.name: storageResourceGroupNameOverride
elements.label: Storage Resource Group Name
elements.toolTip: Optional. Explicit storage resource group name. The placeholder previews the standard convention; leave blank to generate the name.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid resource group name or leave blank to use the generated name.

elements.name: deploymentResourceGroupNameOverride
elements.label: Temporary Deployment Resource Group Name
elements.toolTip: Optional. Explicit temporary deployment resource group name. The placeholder previews the standard convention; leave blank to generate the name.

constraints.validationMessage: Enter a valid resource group name or leave blank to use the generated name.

elements.name: deploymentVirtualMachineNameOverride
elements.label: Temporary Deployment VM Name
elements.toolTip: Optional. Explicit temporary deployment VM name. The generated name removes separators, adds a unique suffix, and is truncated to 15 characters; leave blank to generate it.

constraints.validationMessage: Use 1-15 letters, numbers, or dashes, or leave blank to use the generated name.

elements.name: deploymentVirtualMachineDiskNameOverride
elements.label: Temporary Deployment VM OS Disk Name
elements.toolTip: Optional. Explicit OS disk name. Replace {vmName} with the temporary deployment VM name, or leave blank to derive the disk name from the generated VM name.

elements.name: deploymentVirtualMachineNicNameOverride
elements.label: Temporary Deployment VM NIC Name
elements.toolTip: Optional. Explicit network interface name. Replace {vmName} with the temporary deployment VM name, or leave blank to derive the NIC name from the generated VM name.

elements.name: deploymentUserAssignedIdentityNameOverride
elements.label: Temporary Deployment Identity Name
elements.toolTip: Optional. Explicit name for the temporary deployment user-assigned identity. The placeholder previews the standard convention; leave blank to generate the name.

constraints.validationMessage: Use 3-128 letters, numbers, dashes, or underscores, or leave blank to use the generated name.

elements.name: storageAccountNamePrefixOverride
elements.label: Azure Files Storage Account Name Prefix
elements.toolTip: Optional. Lowercase alphanumeric prefix for Azure Files storage accounts. The naming engine appends a generated six-character value by default, and the deployment appends a two-digit storage index to this prefix.

constraints.validationMessage: Use 1-13 lowercase letters or numbers so the two-digit index remains AD-compatible, or leave blank to use the generated prefix.

elements.name: privateEndpointNameConventionOverride
elements.label: Private Endpoint Naming Convention
elements.toolTip: Optional. Naming convention for private endpoints. RESOURCE, SUBRESOURCE, and VNETID are replaced at deployment time and must remain in the convention.

constraints.validationMessage: Include the RESOURCE, SUBRESOURCE, and VNETID tokens, or leave blank to use the generated convention.

elements.name: privateEndpointNicNameConventionOverride
elements.label: Private Endpoint NIC Naming Convention
elements.toolTip: Optional. Naming convention for private endpoint network interfaces. RESOURCE, SUBRESOURCE, and VNETID are replaced at deployment time and must remain in the convention.

constraints.validationMessage: Include the RESOURCE, SUBRESOURCE, and VNETID tokens, or leave blank to use the generated convention.

elements.name: encryptionUserAssignedIdentityNameOverride
elements.label: Storage Encryption Identity Name
elements.toolTip: Optional. Explicit name for the Azure Files encryption identity. The placeholder previews the standard convention; leave blank to generate the name.

constraints.validationMessage: Use 3-128 letters, numbers, dashes, or underscores, or leave blank to use the generated name.

elements.name: netAppAccountNameOverride
elements.label: New Azure NetApp Files Account Name
elements.toolTip: Optional. Explicit Azure NetApp Files account name. The placeholder previews the standard convention; leave blank to generate the name.

elements.name: netAppCapacityPoolNameOverride
elements.label: New Azure NetApp Files Capacity Pool Name
elements.toolTip: Optional. Explicit Azure NetApp Files capacity pool name. The placeholder previews the standard convention; leave blank to generate the name.

elements.name: smbServerLocationOverride
elements.label: SMB Server Location Token
elements.toolTip: Optional. Short location token used in the Azure NetApp Files SMB server name (for example, use2). Leave blank to use the naming engine's abbreviation for the selected region.
